[[File:Yucca glori.JPG|thumb]]
'''''Yucca gloriosa''''', also known as '''Spanish dagger''', '''mound lily yucca''' and [[#Names|other common names]], is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[asparagus family]], [[native plant|native]] to the southeastern United States. Growing to {{convert|2.5|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}, it is an [[evergreen]] shrub. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental for its architectural qualities, and has reportedly become established in warmer climates in the wild in various parts of the world.

==Description==
''Yucca gloriosa'' is [[Wikt:caulescent|caulescent]], usually with several stems arising from the base, the base thickening in adult specimens. The long narrow leaves are straight and very stiff, growing to {{convert|30|-|50|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2-3.5|cm|in|frac=4|abbr=on}} wide. They are dark green with entire margins, smooth, rarely finely denticulate, [[acuminate]], with a sharp brown terminal spine. The inflorescence is a [[panicle]] up to {{convert|2.5|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} long, of bell-shaped white flowers, sometimes tinged purple or red. The fruit is a leathery, elongate berry up to {{convert|8|cm|in|frac=2|abbr=on}} long.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242102065 Flora of North America v 26 p 429]</ref><ref>[http://www.botanicus.org/page/358338 Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753.  Species Plantarum 1: 319.]</ref><ref>Wunderlin, R. P. 1998. Guide to the Vascular Plants of Florida i–x, 1–806. University Press of Florida, Gainesville.</ref><ref>Radford, A. E., H. E. Ahles & C. R. Bell. 1968. Manual of the Vascular Flora of the Carolinas i–lxi, 1–1183. University of North Carolina Press, Chapel Hill.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Yucca gloriosa'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753.<ref name=IPNI_325010-2>{{IPNI |mode=cs1 |taxon=Yucca gloriosa |authority=L.. |id=325010-2 |access-date=2023-10-05}}</ref> Genetic evidence has shown that the species originated via multiple hybridizations between ''[[Yucca aloifolia]]'' and ''[[Yucca filamentosa]]''.<ref name=HeydMcAsGrimShu21>{{Citation |last1=Heyduk |first1=Karolina |last2=McAssey |first2=Edward V. |last3=Grimwood |first3=Jane |last4=Shu |first4=Shengqiang |last5=Schmutz |first5=Jeremy |last6=McKain |first6=Michael R. |last7=Leebens-Mack |first7=Jim |date=2021 |title=Hybridization History and Repetitive Element Content in the Genome of a Homoploid Hybrid, Yucca gloriosa (Asparagaceae) |journal=Frontiers in Plant Science |volume=11 |article-number=573767 |doi=10.3389/fpls.2020.573767 |pmid=33519836 |name-list-style=amp |doi-access=free |pmc=7843428 |bibcode=2021FrPS...1173767H }}</ref> It is classified as part of the ''[[Yucca]]'' genus within the [[Asparagaceae]] family.<ref name="POWO" />

The species has two accepted [[Variety (botany)|varieties]]:<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id=325010-2 |title=''Yucca gloriosa'' L. |access-date=26 September 2025}}</ref>

* ''Yucca gloriosa'' var. ''gloriosa''
* ''Yucca gloriosa'' var. ''tristis'' {{small|Carrière}}

''Yucca gloriosa'' has {{table row counter|id=Synonyms}} [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]] of the species or one of its two varieties including 28 species.<ref name="POWO" /><ref name="POWO var gloriosa">{{cite POWO |id=77169219-1 |title=''Yucca gloriosa'' var. ''gloriosa'' |access-date=26 September 2025}}</ref><ref name="POWO var tristis">{{cite POWO |id=270369-2 |title=''Yucca gloriosa'' var. ''tristis'' Carrière |access-date=26 September 2025}}</ref>

In addition to Spanish dagger and mound lily yucca,<ref name="Irish">{{Cite book |last1=Irish |first1=Mary |last2=Irish |first2=Gary |date=2000 |title=Agaves, Yuccas, and Related Plants: A Gardener's Guide |url=https://archive.org/details/agavesyuccasrela0000iris |url-access=registration |language=en |location=Portland, Oregon |publisher=Timber Press |page=254 |isbn=978-0-88192-442-8 |oclc=41966994 |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> ''Yucca gloriosa'' is also commonly known as Roman candle,<ref name="Timber Press">{{Cite book |last1=Timber Press |date=2003 |editor-last1=Barnard |editor-first1=Loretta |editor-last2=Doggett |editor-first2=Dannielle |editor-last3=Doig |editor-first3=Fiona |editor-last4=Etherington |editor-first4=Kate |title=Flora's Plant Names |url=https://archive.org/details/florasplantnames00glob |url-access=registration |language=en |location=Portland, Oregon |publisher=Timber Press |pages=66, 192, 223 |isbn=978-0-88192-605-7 |oclc=52948957 |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> palm lily,<ref name="Timber Press"/> and Spanish needle.<ref name="Timber Press"/>  However all of these names are ambiguous, with Roman candle also referring to ''[[Senna alata]]''<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Skerrett |first1=Adrian |last2=Skerrett |first2=Judith |date=1991 |title=The Beautiful Plants of Seychelles |url=https://archive.org/details/beautifulplantso0000sker |url-access=registration |language=en |location=Nairobi, Kenya |publisher=Camerapix Publishers International |pages=66, 192, 223 |isbn=978-1-874041-05-4 |oclc=31901071 |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> or a trade name for a ''[[Podocarpus macrophyllus]]'' cultivar, palm lily almost always referring to ''[[Cordyline fruticosa]]''<ref>{{GRIN | name = ''Cordyline fruticosa'' (L.) A. Chev. | id = 401621| access-date = 3 March 2026 }}</ref> or other ''[[Cordyline]]''s, and Spanish needle also referring to ''[[Bidens alba]]''.<ref>Linda C. Duever. [https://floridata.com/plant/898 "#898 ''Bidens alba''."] ''Floridata.'' 21 November 2003. Retrieved 30 March 2026.</ref>

In the horticultural trade, ''[[Yucca gloriosa var. tristis]]'' varieties, with their less rigid leaves, are often referred to as ''Y. pendula'' or ''Y. recurvifolia'', and commonly called '''soft-leaf'''<ref>{{cite web | title=Yucca recurvifolia - Soft-leaf yucca |url=https://www.unf.edu/botanical-garden/plants/yucca-recurvifolia.html |website=UNF Botanical Garden |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> (or '''soft-tipped'''<ref name="Irish"/>) '''yucca''', '''weeping yucca''',<ref>{{cite web |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/yucca-gloriosa-var-tristis/ |title=''Yucca gloriosa'' var. ''tristis'' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |publisher=N. C. Cooperative Extension |access-date=30 March 2026 }}</ref> '''curve-leaf yucca'''<ref>{{cite usda plants|symbol=YURE2|title=''Yucca recurvifolia'' Salisb.|access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> or '''curved-leaved Spanish-dagger'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref>

==Habitat==
''Yucca gloriosa'' grows on exposed [[sand dune]]s along the coast and [[barrier island]]s of the lower [[East Coast of the United States]], often together with ''[[Yucca aloifolia]]'' and a variety formerly called ''Yucca recurvifolia'' or ''Y. gloriosa'' var. ''recurvifolia'', now ''Y. gloriosa'' var. ''tristis''. Large, endemic populations can be found in the beach and dune environments of coastal [[North Carolina]].<ref name=WCSP>{{Citation |title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families |publisher=The Board of Trustees of the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/home.do |access-date=2012-02-23 }}, search for "Yucca recurvifolia"</ref> In contrast to ''Y. gloriosa'' var. ''tristis'', the leaves of ''Y. gloriosa'' var. ''gloriosa'' are hard stiff, erect and narrower. On the other hand, ''Y. aloifolia'' has leaves with denticulate margins and a sharp-pointed, terminal spine.<!--The flowering period is the end of summer and autumn whereas ''Y. recurvifolia'' blooms in spring. ==Distribution==
''Yucca gloriosa'' is native to the coast and [[barrier island]]s of southeastern North America, growing on [[sand dune]]s. It ranges from extreme southeastern [[Virginia]] south to northern [[Florida]] in the [[United States]]. It is associated with ''[[Yucca filamentosa]]'', ''Yucca aloifolia'', and ''[[Opuntia]]'' species.

==Cultivation==
The plant is widely cultivated in warm [[temperateness|temperate]] and [[subtropical]] climates, and valued as an architectural focal point. It has reportedly escaped from cultivation and naturalised in Italy, Turkey, Mauritius, Réunion, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, Argentina, Chile and Uruguay.<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=291793 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Yucca gloriosa'']</ref>
In landscape use, little maintenance is needed other than the removal of dead leaves when the shrub nears its ultimate height. The plant is very hardy, without leaf damage at {{convert|-20|C|F|abbr=on}}, and can handle brief snow and freezing temperatures, as well as long periods of drought.<ref name="Cae">{{Cite web|url=http://cals.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Yucca_gloriosa.html|title=cals.arizona.edu|access-date=1 March 2007|archive-date=7 September 2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040907050528/http://cals.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Yucca_gloriosa.html}}</ref> 

''Yucca gloriosa'',<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Yucca gloriosa''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/19168/Yucca-gloriosa/Details | publisher = RHS | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> and the [[cultivar]]s 'Variegata'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Yucca gloriosa'' 'Variegata'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/65193/Yucca-gloriosa-Variegata-(v)/Details | publisher = RHS | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> and {{tdes|'''Bright Star'''}} = 'Walbristar'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/274607/i-Yucca-gloriosa-i-Font-Face-times-New-Roman-Bright-Star-FONT-Walbristar-sup-(PBR)-sup-(v)/Details | title = {{tdes|'''Bright Star'''}} = 'Walbristar' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 11 March 2019}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 108 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 10 March 2019}}</ref>

==Properties==
''Yucca gloriosa'' has been known to cause skin irritation and even [[allergy|allergic]] [[Adverse drug reaction|reaction]]s upon contact. The leaf points are even sharp enough to break the skin.<ref name="hce">{{Cite web|url=http://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheets/HGIC1077.htm|title=hgic.clemson.edu|access-date=1 March 2007|archive-date=3 March 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070303112604/http://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheets/HGIC1077.htm}}</ref>
